author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Spotify: ‘Cautious’ Because of the Competition
text:
Photo: Getty Images By David Marino-Nachison June 14, 2018 11:35 a.m. ET Amazon.com , Apple and Google have two main advantages over streaming music star Spotify Technology (SPOT): Financial flexibility and built-in access to new customer streams.
“The competitive landscape could increasingly becoming a headwind to Spotify’s user growth story,” Deutsche Bank analysts wrote Wednesday as they started coverage of the company with a “hold” rating and a $155 price target that’s below current levels.
Deutsche Bank said it was “cautious” about Spotify despite general optimism about streaming music, citing concerns about the possibility of margin growth and competition. The competitive advantages Amazon.com (AMZN), Apple (AAPL) and Alphabet -owned (GOOGL) Google currently have, according to Deutsche Bank:
• They can run their streaming music businesses at a loss.
“While Spotify needs to begin proving to investors that it can achieve its long-term margin profile, Apple/Amazon/Google can continue to invest. with the hope that music streaming will drive incremental users into their respective ecosystems,” the analysts wrote.
That could give the other companies pricing power over Spotify, the analysts wrote.
• Their other businesses give them valuable access to potential subscribers.
For Apple and Google, according to Deutsche Bank, that means hardware; for Amazon, it’s Prime; all three have smart speakers, as well as exposure to the growing voice assistant business.
Illustration: Deutsche Bank Investors briefly soured on Spotify’s stock after its first-ever earnings report as a public company, but shares of Spotify are up some 17% in 2018, ahead of the S&P 500 and topping early May highs, since its early April public listing. Wall Street’s mean target price is approximately $176, right around current levels; Deutsche Bank’s target is fifth-lowest of 20, according to FactSet.
